class_evidence: 9 datasets, all used as two classes (Sec 5.1, pp.333-334; Table 2, p.334): Pima, Phoneme, Adult, E-state, Satimage, Forest Cover, Oil, Mammography, Can; Adult also run with SMOTE-NC (Sec 6.1, pp.348-349). The paper focuses on two-class problems; a multiclass use is stated but not run (pp.333-334).
reduced_multiclass: Satimage (6 classes): smallest class vs the other 5 merged (Sec 5.1 item 5, p.333). Forest Cover (7 classes): only Ponderosa Pine and Cottonwood/Willow kept, the other classes dropped (Sec 5.1 item 6, pp.333-334).
smote_explanation: This paper defines the reference rule and changes none of the six decision points: every minority sample is a seed with N/100 points each (a random N% of seeds when N < 100), the partner is drawn from the k = 5 minority nearest neighbours, and lambda ~ U(0,1) on the segment (Sec 4.2, p.328; algorithm, p.329). Generation runs once before training, combined with random undersampling of the majority (Sec 4.3, p.331). SMOTE-NC changes only the distance used to find neighbours and sets nominal values by a vote of the neighbours (Sec 6.1, p.348).
corrections: Forest Cover was cut to two of its seven classes, not merged.
flags: SMOTE-NC (run, binary) and SMOTE-N (proposed only) are extra variants; SMOTE-NC changes Neighbour choice.

class_evidence: 4 datasets (Sec 4, Table 2, p.112): KDDCup-99 with all 5 classes kept (DoS, Probe, Normal, U2R, R2L); Mammography and Phoneme (two-class); Satimage (reduced to two). Results tabulated only for U2R (Table 3, p.113); R2L omitted for space. RIPPER base learner (p.111).
reduced_multiclass: Satimage: smallest class vs the rest merged (p.112). KDDCup-99 not reduced; only DoS and Normal subsampled for size (p.112).
multiclass_how: AdaBoost.M2 core over labels {1..C} (Fig. 1, p.111); on KDDCup-99 SMOTE is applied separately to each minority class (U2R at 100/300/500%, R2L at 100%) (p.112); the other three classes are not oversampled.
smote_explanation: The generator is unchanged SMOTE (Sec 2, p.109), but it runs inside every AdaBoost.M2 round and the synthetic points are discarded after the round (Sec 3, p.110; Fig. 1, p.111). New points are created by sampling seeds from the round's boosting distribution, which the authors say focuses generation on misclassified or boundary minority cases (pp.110, 116). Allocation, partner, placement and the absence of filtering are as in SMOTE.
corrections: Add Seed selection (seeds drawn from the boosting distribution D_t), flagged as debatable.
flags: How seeds are drawn from D_t is not formalised. The formal algorithm names one minority class; multiclass handling comes from AdaBoost.M2 with hand-set per-class amounts, and only U2R results are reported.

class_evidence: All experiments two-class; a multiclass extension is said to be possible but not covered (Sec. 1, PDF p.4). 90 datasets (Abstract): 12 UCI sets plus randomly undersampled copies, 19 KEEL two-class sets and 10 simulated MADELON sets (Sec. 4.4, PDF p.14; Table 2, PDF p.15), plus 5 two-class 2-D toy sets (Figs. 10-14).
reduced_multiclass: Multiclass UCI sources (e.g. breast tissue, ecoli, glass, iris, libra, segment, vehicle, wine) turned into one-vs-rest problems with the smallest class as minority (Sec. 4.4, PDF p.14); KEEL sets are ready-made binary splits (Table 2).
smote_explanation: k-means clusters the whole input space, and only clusters whose majority-to-minority ratio is below a threshold are kept, so seeds are minority points inside minority-dominated clusters (Sec. 3.1, PDF pp.7-8; Algorithm 1). Samples are shared across kept clusters in proportion to their sparsity, so sparse clusters get more (Sec. 3.1, PDF pp.8-9). Inside each cluster plain SMOTE runs on that cluster's points only, so partners come from the same cluster; placement is unchanged and there is no filtering. With one cluster and no threshold the method reduces to SMOTE (Sec. 3.2, PDF p.9).
corrections: Add Neighbour choice (partner restricted to the same cluster). Evidence: 90 datasets (12 UCI plus undersampled variants, 19 KEEL, 10 MADELON).
flags: Neighbour choice debatable: only the candidate pool is restricted. Some minority counts in Table 2 look like merged classes rather than the smallest class.

class_evidence: All experiments two-class: 28 base datasets (13 UCI, 13 KEEL, 2 simulated MADELON) plus undersampled copies, 69 in total (Sec. 5.1, PDF p.18; Table 1, pp.18-19); binary AUC, F-score and G-mean (Sec. 5.2).
reduced_multiclass: Multiclass sources (e.g. iris, wine, glass, vehicle, segmentation, ecoli, libras, vowel, led, dermatology) appear as two-class sets in Table 1; how they were reduced is not stated.
smote_explanation: Seeds and allocation are SMOTE-like (Sec. 4.1, PDF p.9). The surface point that sets the radius is chosen by a selection strategy: a random minority neighbour as in SMOTE, the nearest majority point, or whichever of the two is closer (Algorithm 1, PDF p.8; Sec. 4.3 step 4). The segment is replaced by a point drawn in a hypersphere around the seed with that radius, truncated and deformed into a hyper-spheroid along the seed-to-surface axis (Sec. 4.2; Sec. 4.3 steps 6-9, PDF pp.14-16). With full truncation and deformation and the minority strategy the region becomes SMOTE's segment (Sec. 5.4, PDF p.24).
corrections: Add Neighbour choice: the majority or combined strategy can make a majority point the radius point. Evidence: 13 UCI + 13 KEEL + 2 MADELON, 69 with undersampled copies.
flags: The SMOTE special case gives SMOTE's support (the segment) but probably not its uniform lambda law.
